html:
Cantia, the Latin name for Kent, was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the far southeast of England, shown on the map for 600 and 700. Its kings claimed descent from Hengist and Horsa, Jutish leaders said to have landed in the mid 400s. The map's outline for it is rough and spreads well beyond Kent itself.

Kent faced the Channel and traded closely with the Franks. Its king Æthelberht married a Christian Frankish princess, Bertha. In 597 he received Augustine, sent from Rome in the Gregorian mission, and was baptised. Canterbury became the seat of the English church, as it still is. Æthelberht's laws are the oldest surviving text written in English.

Kent later fell under the power of Mercia in the 700s and passed to Wessex in the 820s, becoming a part of the kingdom that grew into England.
